essence: For years the name Pyrrha meant a castled city cupped above a bay; the moment Marco set foot in the real place, a low, dusty town of sawmills and windpumps took the name for good, leaving the imagined city intact but nameless.
textDetails: Before his visit, Marco long pictured Pyrrha as a castled, fortified town built on the hillsides above a bay.
His imagined Pyrrha had tall windows set high up, and towers.
The whole town closed in on itself like a cup or goblet.
At its centre lay a square sunk as deep as a shaft, with a well in the middle of it.
He had not seen it: Pyrrha was one of many places he knew only through their names and furnished in imagination; the others he lists are Euphrasia, Odile, Margara and Getullia.
Among those name-cities Pyrrha stood apart from each of the others, yet like each it was perfectly distinct to his inner eye.
When he finally travelled there, the imagined town vanished at his first step; Pyrrha simply became itself, and he felt he had known it all along.
From the real town the sea is out of sight, masked by a dune along a low, undulating shore.
Its streets are long and run dead straight.
The houses are low and gathered in separate clusters, with open yards between them holding piled lumber and sawmills.
The wind spins the bladed wheels of water pumps (the Italian 'girandole', literally pinwheels).
Ever since, the name has summoned that particular view, that light, a constant buzzing and air full of drifting yellowish dust, and he cannot imagine it meaning anything else.
His mind still stores many unvisited cities as names, each carrying a figure, a fragment or a flicker of an imagined figure.

The first imagined town, high over its bay with its square closed round the well, still exists in his mind, but it has lost its name, and he cannot recall how he ever gave it one that now signifies something else entirely.
visualConcept: One floating island, two Pyrrhas that hold the name in turn. By default we see the Pyrrha Marco found: a low, gently rolling coastal plain in hazy yellow light, with a long sand dune along the back edge hiding the sea from the town (only from the camera's height does a thin blade of sea glint beyond the crest). Long straight streets run edge to edge and vanish into the dust; low whitewashed houses huddle in separate clumps, and between the clumps lie open lots stacked with lumber, sawdust heaps and open-sided sawmill sheds with spinning circular blades, while tall lattice windpumps with many-bladed rotors whirl and swing to face the wind and yellowish dust streams through everything. A gilt plaque reading PYRRHA stands at the head of the main street: this is where the name now lives. High above the hidden sea, small and translucent like a thought, floats the other Pyrrha: a castled city cupped on the hillsides above a bay, towers with tall windows along its rim and a square sunk like a well with a well at its heart, rendered in cool lapis glass with candle-lit windows and carrying a blank plaque. Around it hang four fainter glints, the unseen cities Marco knows only by name (Euphrasia, Odile, Margara, Getullia), each no more than a figure, a fragment or a spark with its name in fine gilt. The toggle runs the journey backwards and forwards: the plain lifts into slopes around a bay, the cup-city descends and grows to full size, the name glides onto it, and arrival wipes it all away again.
layout: Island radius 22, ground at y=0. Real state: a plain with gentle undulation (amplitude 0.3); a dune ridge along the north edge (z from -15 to -19), 2.2 high and smooth; beyond it a 3-unit strip of sea at y=0.1, visible only from above. Five long parallel streets run east-west at z = -9, -4, 1, 6 and 11, each crossing the whole island and fading into fog at both ends; two straight cross streets at x = -7 and x = 8. Eight clumps of 6-10 low houses (0.7-1.3 tall, one or two storeys, pale whitewash, shallow tiled roofs), clumps at least 4 units apart; between them 6 lumber lots (neat stacks of instanced planks and logs, 0.5-1 high) and 4 sawmill sheds (open-sided, 3 by 2, 1.4 tall, each with a 0.6-wide spinning blade, a log carriage and a sawdust cone). Twelve windpumps along the streets: lattice towers 3.2-4 tall, an 18-blade rotor 1.3 across, a tail vane, and a water tank or trough at the foot. 25 tiny people and 3 mule carts. The PYRRHA plaque (gilt, 1.6 wide) on two posts at the west end of the z=1 street. Imagined state (same island, terrain heightfield morphed): a bay of deep water cutting in from the north edge (radius about 9, centred at (0, 0, -16)), slopes rising steeply to a hilltop centred at (0, 0, 3); on it the cup-shaped walled city: ring wall of radius 6.5 at height 6-7 with 12 towers 4-5 tall pierced by slit windows set high up, houses in four tiers stepping down the inner slope toward the centre, and a central square that is a cylindrical pit of radius 1.5 and depth 3 with a round wellhead at the bottom. Floating remnant (real state): the same cup-city at scale 0.18 hovering at (0, 9, -21) over the hidden sea, with the four name-glints on a loose ring of radius 4-6 around it.
signatureMotion: 1) Wind: a steady breeze keeps every windpump rotor whirling (with gusts), swings all the tail vanes together when the wind veers every 20-30 s, ripples the dune sand, and drives a stream of about 4,000 yellowish dust particles along the long streets with a fine vibrating jitter that reads as buzzing; the sawmill blades spin and spit sawdust. 2) The remembered city: the small lapis cup-city high over the dune bobs and turns very slowly, its windows flickering like candles and its blank plaque catching the light, while the four name-glints twinkle in turn. 3) The arrival transition (on toggle, about 5 s): the terrain heightfield interpolates, the imagined towers dissolve top-down in a dithered fade while the windpump towers rise in their places, the bay drains behind a rising dune, the sky shifts from clear blue to dusty yellow, and the PYRRHA plaque glides between the two cities.
interactionDescription: Rewinds to before the journey. The dust settles, the windpumps and sawmills sink and dissolve, the plain lifts into steep slopes around a blue bay, and the small floating cup-city descends and swells into a full-size castled city with towers, high windows and a well-deep square; the gilt PYRRHA plaque leaves the main street and settles on its gate, and the light turns clear and blue. Toggle off and you arrive: in a single step the imagined city is forgotten, the dusty town returns, the name moves back down to it, and the cup-city shrinks to a small, nameless image hanging over the hidden sea.
mood: Real Pyrrha: a windy, hot late afternoon; a low sun through a haze of fine yellow dust, everything washed in straw and ochre with soft long shadows; the air seems to hum with saws, wind and insects, and heat shimmers above the roads. Imagined Pyrrha: the clear, still blue hour of a dream, crisp air, the bay mirror-calm and glinting, warm candlelight in high windows; cooler, sharper and more theatrical.
caption: Until you go there, the name Pyrrha holds a castled town cupped on the slopes above a bay, all towers and tall windows, its square sunk like a shaft, a wellhead at the bottom. Then you arrive. A dune keeps the sea out of sight, straight roads run on and on, low houses huddle between timber yards and sawmills, pumps whirl, yellow dust hangs in the air. The name means only this now; the other town floats on, unnamed.
motto: Arrive once, and a name forgets everything it used to mean.
camera: Distance about 38, elevation about 24 degrees, target (0, 1.5, -2), camera placed to the south-east (about 35 degrees off the north-south axis) looking north-west across the town, so the east-west streets cut diagonally through the frame, the dune ridge runs across the back, and the small floating cup-city hovers just above the dune crest in the upper third. In the imagined state the camera eases back to distance 42 and up to 28 degrees to take in the bay and the full cup-city.
